## 2. Timestamp and clock-shift checks

IST (Asia/Kolkata, UTC+05:30) has no DST so no ambiguous or non-existent hours can arise.
The following checks were applied to `load_raw_hourly.parquet`:

| Check | Result | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate timestamps | **0** | No action needed |
| Non-hour-aligned timestamps (minute ≠ 0 or second ≠ 0) | **0** | No action needed |
| Unexpected step between consecutive timestamps (clock shifts) | **0** | No action needed |
| Missing hours in hourly index | **455** (spread across 241 gap episodes) | Reindexed to complete grid; NaNs imputed (§3) |

The complete hourly `ts` index runs from `2023-04-01 00:00:00+05:30` to `2026-01-12 23:00:00+05:30` with no gaps.

## 3. Missing data and imputation

### 3.1 Gap-length distribution (before imputation)

| Gap length (hours) | Episodes | Hours affected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 212 | 212 |
| 2 | 6 | 12 |
| 3 | 5 | 15 |
| 4 | 1 | 4 |
| 5 | 3 | 15 |
| 6 | 1 | 6 |
| 7 | 3 | 21 |
| 8 | 2 | 16 |
| 10 | 1 | 10 |
| 12 | 3 | 36 |
| 13 | 1 | 13 |
| 14 | 1 | 14 |
| 32 | 1 | 32 |
| 49 | 1 | 49 |
| **Total** | **241** | **455** |

The largest gap is **49 hours** (2 days + 1 hour). The longest contiguous run without any gap is over 1,000 hours.

### 3.2 Imputation rules

| Config key | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cleaning.linear_gap_max_hours` | 3 | Gaps ≤ 3 h → linear interpolation |
| `cleaning.hour_of_week_weeks` | 4 | Gaps > 3 h → mean of nearest 4 non-missing same-hour-of-week |

**Linear interpolation** (`imputation_method = "linear"`):
Applied to all gap episodes of length 1–3 h (223 episodes, 239 hours).
Boundary values on each side are known and the demand signal varies smoothly within a few hours.

**Hour-of-week fill** (`imputation_method = "hour_of_week"`):
Applied to all gap episodes of length > 3 h (18 episodes, 216 hours, up to the 49-h episode).
For each missing timestamp $t$, the imputed value is the mean of the nearest 4 non-missing observations at the same (day-of-week, hour) pair, found by scanning $t \pm 1\text{ week}, \pm 2\text{ weeks}, \ldots$ until 4 non-null values are collected.

### 3.3 Imputation summary

| Method | Hours imputed | Percent of total |
|---|---|---|
| `linear` | 239 | 0.978 % |
| `hour_of_week` | 216 | 0.884 % |
| None (observed) | 23,977 | 98.138 % |
| **Total** | **24,432** | **100 %** |

**No NaN values remain in `load_mw` after imputation.**

## 4. Outlier / outage-suspect flagging

**Method:** Robust z-score of the residual against the global hour-of-week (HOW) median profile.

For each timestamp $t$:
$$r_t = \text{load\_mw}(t) - \text{median}\bigl(\{\text{load\_mw}(t') \mid \text{how}(t') = \text{how}(t)\}\bigr)$$
$$z_t = \frac{\lvert r_t - \text{median}(r) \rvert}{\text{MAD}(r)}, \quad \text{MAD}(r) = \text{median}\bigl(\lvert r - \text{median}(r) \rvert\bigr)$$
Flag `is_outage_suspect = True` when $z_t \ge \text{cleaning.outage\_mad\_z} = 6.0$.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| Global HOW-residual MAD | 965.52 MW |
| Maximum observed robust z | 4.1955 |
| `is_outage_suspect = True` | **0 rows** |

**Result: no rows were flagged.**

The Delhi load signal spans 2023-04 to 2026-01, exhibiting a large annual seasonal swing (~1,500 MW in deep winter to ~8,500 MW at summer peak). Because the global hour-of-week median profile is a single all-year profile, the residuals absorb the full inter-seasonal variation (~±3,000 MW), pushing the global MAD to ~966 MW. A threshold of 6.0 × 966 MW = 5,796 MW would require a load of roughly −1,296 MW or +11,296 MW — physically impossible. The maximum observed z is **4.20**, well below the threshold.

**Decision:** Implement the specification exactly and report zero suspects. The `outage_mad_z` threshold is a suitable guard against gross data corruption or telemetry faults that may appear in future data refreshes or in other grid datasets. No rows are altered.

**Three largest residuals (by z-score) for reference:**

| Timestamp | load_mw (MW) | HOW residual (MW) | Robust z |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-06-19 00:00 IST | 8,128.0 | +4,050.8 | 4.1955 |
| 2024-06-19 01:00 IST | 7,863.0 | +4,022.4 | 4.1660 |
| 2024-06-18 23:00 IST | 8,272.5 | +4,009.8 | 4.1530 |

These are peak-demand hours during the June 2024 heatwave — legitimate extreme-but-real demand, not outage drops.
